resources.string: Performs the taps, swipes and typing in flows you create and start.

AutoFlow uses this accessibility service only to perform the taps, swipes, long presses, scrolls, typing and system actions (such as Back or Home) that you put into your own flows, and to show a floating Stop button while a flow runs. It looks at the screen only to find the text field you type into or an element your flow targets. It does not collect, store or share what is on your screen, it never acts on lock, permission or Settings screens, and it acts only when you start a flow or a trigger you set up fires. You can stop any run at any time.
Shows a flow while it runs, with Stop and Pause.
Notifications sent by your flows\' notify steps.
Yes/No questions asked by your flows\' confirm steps.

AutoFlow is an automation app. To run the flows you create, it uses Android's Accessibility Service API.

What AutoFlow accesses and why:
• Screen actions: it performs the taps, swipes, long presses, scrolls, typing and system actions (Back, Home, Recents) that you put into your flows.
• Screen content: it reads the text and layout of the window in front to find the element or text field a step targets, and to see which app is open for app triggers, key profiles and the protected-screen guard.
• Keys you press: on a hardware keyboard, only when you have set up hotkeys or key mappings.
• Text you type: only while you record a flow, so it can add a typing step. Password fields are never read.

This data is processed only on your device. AutoFlow does not collect it, send it to us or share it with anyone, and does not use it for ads. Text you record is saved only in that flow.

AutoFlow never acts on the lock screen, permission dialogs or system Settings, and it acts only when you start a flow or a trigger you set up fires. You can turn the service off any time in Settings › Accessibility.

Tap "Agree" to open Android Settings and turn on "AutoFlow automations".
